status: FINAL — capability report, not a deployment gate
note: This file is deliberately not logs/eye/validation_report.json. The eye module remains validation_failed. Promotion is a human decision under roadmap step 6.

claim.task: Referable diabetic retinopathy: ICDR grade >= 2 versus grade < 2, as a binary referral signal on a single fundus photograph.
what_this_does_not_cover: Mild DR. Grade 1 versus grade 0 is a separate task and is NOT supported by this report. Measured separately in roadmap step 2 at AUC 0.660 [0.617, 0.703] with a dedicated head -- real signal, but not screening-usable, and nothing here changes that.
DR severity grading. Exact-grade accuracy on this same set is 0.267 and quadratic weighted kappa 0.460; the module cannot assign a grade.
Any non-DR condition. Glaucoma, cataract, AMD and the rest are outside this claim, and their apparently strong numbers elsewhere are within-source, not external.
Diagnosis. This is a triage signal that decides who is seen sooner, not what they have.

evaluation_population.cross_source: different acquisition source from APTOS and ODIR, both of which are in training
evaluation_population.sampling: stratified 300 per grade, so referable disease is over-represented threefold relative to the source population

metrics.calibration_warning: ranks well, not calibrated: see limitations. Discrimination (AUC) and calibration are independent, and only the first is established here.

limitations: No operating point is selected. Every threshold above was read off this same set; choosing one here and quoting its sensitivity would be selection on the test data. A deployment threshold must be fixed on a separate selection set before any promotion.
PPV on this set is inflated. It is 60% referable by construction against 19.6% in full EyePACS, so the per-threshold PPV at natural prevalence is the honest figure and is reported beside it.
One external source. EyePACS is US-based; the module has no measured performance on any other unseen population.
Single-image, single-field. No stereo, no fundus pairs, no clinical context, and no assessment of image-quality gating in deployment.
Nondeterminism: inference on this GPU drifts run to run at roughly 1e-5 AUC (roadmap step 1). Immaterial here, but it means figures quoted to four decimals from a single run are over-precise.
Grade labels are EyePACS's own single-grader ICDR labels, which are known to carry grader noise; no adjudicated subset was available.

THE SCORE IS NOT CALIBRATED. It ranks well but is not a probability: Brier 0.268, 46.9% of scores below 0.01, and the thresholds reaching 80-95% sensitivity all sit between 0.000 and 0.005. A default 0.5 cut would refer almost nothing. The raw number must never be displayed as a percentage risk, and calibration on a separate set is a prerequisite for any deployment, not a refinement.
deployment_claim_if_promoted: May be offered ONLY as: a worklist ordering aid that ranks fundus photographs by likelihood of referable DR (ICDR >= 2) so a human reviewer sees higher-risk images sooner. Every image in the queue is still reviewed by a person; the model changes the order, not the outcome. It issues no refer/no-refer verdict, discharges nobody, and its score is not a probability. Validated on one external source (EyePACS, n=1,500) against single-grader labels; not validated on any other population.

framing_decision.rationale: The same AUC supports one claim and not the other. AUC measures ranking; it says nothing about where a threshold belongs or what a positive means at a given prevalence. As a decision rule this model fails: at 90% sensitivity it flags 70% of all images and its PPV at the real 19.6% prevalence is 0.353, so two referrals in three would be unnecessary, and lowering sensitivity to 80% only reaches 0.506. As a ranking it works: the top 20% of the queue holds 71.2% of referable disease. The tool orders a reviewer's worklist; it does not decide anyone's care.
what_this_forbids: Reporting a per-image 'refer' or 'no refer' verdict to a patient or a non-specialist.
Discharging, clearing, or de-prioritising a patient on a low score. The claim is about what to look at first, not what can be skipped.
Quoting 0.887 as screening accuracy. It is ranking quality on one external source.
Displaying the raw score as a probability or percentage risk — it is uncalibrated (Brier 0.268, 46.9% of scores below 0.01).

at_natural_prevalence_19_6pc.note: positives subsampled from the frozen set to match EyePACS's real referable prevalence; ranking is unchanged, only the mix

on_frozen_set_as_sampled.note: reported for completeness and to show the artefact: at 60% referable, enrichment is bounded near 1.6x because a majority class cannot be concentrated. This understates deployed value as much as the same set's PPV overstates it.
